records.summary: A consumer directory for software-service users listing region-specific official support routes and when they were last checked. It would help users find a human support channel; it would not contact or call support for them.
records.customer: Consumers trying to reach human customer support
records.paid_demand: The evidence cluster reports 23 paying-proof snippets, but the supplied examples do not establish payment for this directory idea.

competitors.name: GetHuman
competitors.note: Long-running customer-support contact database and tools.

competitors.name: Resolver
competitors.note: Free service that overlaps with contact finding and complaint resolution.

rounds.plain: K0: the directory is easy to copy and GetHuman already offers a comparable asset. K1: SEO distribution is plausible, but the agent-work share and ≤5 h/week are unverified; K4: more than five maintained free services overlap.

risks: No evidenced wedge against free directories and complaint-resolution services.
The supplied Reddit example is truncated before any support complaint, so its relevance is unverified.
Agent-work share and ≤5 h/week are unverified.
records.moat: Weak: public support routes are readily reproducible, and GetHuman already operates a comparable directory.

records.summary: A personal search assistant that would find and summarize information across selected apps using authorized connectors. A browser extension would cover web apps without connectors.
records.customer: People who need to search across selected apps
records.paid_demand: The evidence cluster reports 4 paying-proof snippets out of 21 complainers, but the supplied examples are heterogeneous and do not establish payment for this assistant.

rounds.plain: K0: common connectors and retrieval workflows appear copyable, and major providers already offer cross-app search. K1: operating-hours and agent-work requirements are unverified; K2: two dated competing launches were found; K3: platform owners and providers already serve this need.

risks: Connector delivery time and integration approvals are unverified.
No exclusive data or access was verified.
Only 4 of 21 evidence snippets had paying proof; the examples are heterogeneous.
records.moat: Weak: common connectors and retrieval workflows appear copyable, and established providers already offer cross-app search.

records.customer: People who need help using web apps
records.paid_demand: The evidence cluster reports 4 paying-proof snippets out of 19 complainers. One supplied post says, “I would pay for this,” but does not document an actual purchase.

records.summary: A browser extension for blocking ads and unwanted content. It would give users controls and use maintained filter lists.
records.customer: Browser users who want to block ads and unwanted content
records.paid_demand: The evidence cluster reports 7 paying-proof snippets out of 18 complainers, but the supplied examples do not establish payment for this extension.

competitors.name: uBlock Origin
competitors.note: Free maintained option; community maintains widely used filter lists.

rounds.plain: K0: a comparable extension using existing filter lists has no demonstrated copying barrier or exclusive asset. K1: automation and ≤5 owner hours per week are unverified; K2: three competing launches are listed; K3: browser makers provide built-in blockers; K4: at least six free or low-cost maintained options exist.

risks: No distinct wedge surfaced for browser ads.
The extension would not cover ads inside unrelated native apps.
Automation and ≤5 owner hours per week are unverified.
records.moat: Weak: widely used filter lists are maintained by uBlock Origin’s community, and browser makers provide built-in blockers.
